Outlet: CNBC, published Friday November 6 2026 9:02 AM EST, updated 11:29 AM EST. By Oliver Renick
Wall Street's fear gauge may be flashing a buy sign

VIX surged more than 11 points from 16.6 to 28.2 on Thursday, marking its largest one-day move since April 2025.
Following 19 instances since 1990 when the VIX rose at least five points from under 20, the median S&P 500 return was 4.2% three months later and 4.8% six months later; positive 68% of the time over three months and 79% over six months. One-month: median return 2.1%, average return negative 0.4%.
Nasdaq 100 posted worst day since March 2020. VXN (Nasdaq Volatility Index) jumped over 13 points to 38.3, highest since April 11, 2025. S&P 500 lost 4% on Thursday; Nasdaq 100 lost 6%.
Semiconductor ETF (SMH) options: 670,000 puts traded of 900,000 total options; $1.5 billion of $1.7 billion premium in puts.

Paul Hickey, co-founder of Bespoke Investment Group: "These types of sharp spikes from placid levels are like a line of thunderstorms coming through in summer" with quick darkening skies and temporary disturbances.
